summary: Your people or theirs: You are the new executive, and the people who run the departments, or the body that confirms them, are not yours.
realLife: One life: Elected Burlington, Vermont, mayor by about ten votes in 1981 as an independent, he faced a board where most members opposed him. They fired his secretary and rejected nearly all his appointees; he sued, lost, then worked out a compromise. Another: After beating the incumbent mayor of Wasilla, Alaska, in 1996, she asked the department heads for resignation letters and fired the police chief, who sued; the suit was dismissed.
gates: You hold an executive office (mayor, county executive, governor) in your first months.
weights: How many members of the body are on the other side.
How openly each head backed your opponent.
choices: keep each head, ask for a resignation letter to hold, or let them go
